title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
abstract: arXiv:2611.31227v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components. Building on this principle, we introduce BiPert, a simple linear framework for both forward perturbation prediction and inverse identification. For forward prediction, BiPert outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge when predicting gene expression changes in unseen cell lines. translated_title: 线性模型能走多远？BiPert：一个用于单细胞扰动建模的统一框架
translated_abstract: 理解基因扰动如何影响细胞行为，对于研究基因功能和调控机制至关重要。大规模CRISPR筛选能够测量数千个基因上的这些效应，但仅覆盖相对较少的细胞背景。因此，在未见过的细胞类型中预测扰动响应，以及从转录效应中识别被扰动的基因，仍然具有挑战性。在本研究中，我们证明这两项任务都可以通过一种通用的线性分解来解决，即将转录响应分解为共享成分和扰动特异性成分。基于这一原理，我们提出了BiPert，一个用于正向扰动预测和逆向识别的简单线性框架。在正向预测方面，BiPert在不使用外部生物学知识的情况下，在预测未见细胞系中的基因表达变化时优于现有方法。其少样本扩展版本BiPert-FS能够仅使用极少的样本适应新的细胞系……
tldr: 提出BiPert，一个简单的线性框架，通过将转录响应分解为共享与扰动特异性成分，统一解决了单细胞扰动建模中的正向响应预测和逆向扰动基因识别两项任务。
en_tdlr: BiPert is a simple linear framework that decomposes transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components, unifying forward perturbation prediction and inverse perturbation identification in single-cell modelling.
